t: Network Policy Validator - public implementations survey
title: Network Policy Validator - public implementations survey
definition: Checks rules for conflicts and unintended exposure.
description:
Network Policy Validator is one of the fundamental capabilities an AI needs to build things on demand: Checks rules for conflicts and unintended exposure. In the real world this capability is delivered by a rich ecosystem of tools, libraries and platforms. This database is the public edition - a fact-checked survey of the real implementations, the real techniques they share, the standards they follow, and laddered drills that teach the capability hands-on.

No single tool owns Network Policy Validator. Competing implementations emphasize different trade-offs: speed against flexibility, simplicity against power, integration against independence. The implementation spotlights in this database document the notable real ones - what each does, where it excels, and how it serves Network Policy Validator. Together they map the territory as it actually exists.

Every record carries a runnable demonstration program, because tools are understood by use. Run the demos with node, compare the implementations, practice the drills, and the Network Policy Validator capability becomes something you can reach for - with full knowledge of which real tool fits which job.

t: TCP/IP - related Network Policy Validator technology
title: TCP/IP - related Network Policy Validator technology
definition: The internet's packet protocols.
description:
TCP/IP is not itself a Network Policy Validator, but it belongs in this survey because real Network Policy Validator work leans on it. The internet's packet protocols.

In a Network Policy Validator build it shows up when the team already lives in its ecosystem. Its architecture reflects hard-won lessons: small sharp pieces, explicit contracts between them, and no magic hidden from the operator. Knowing the surrounding technology is part of knowing the capability - the best Network Policy Validator practitioners can say exactly where their tool ends and its neighbors begin.

For builders, TCP/IP is worth evaluating first as supporting technology. The demo program exercises a core idea from its domain - run it with node and watch each step.

t: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Network Policy Va
title: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Network Policy Va
definition: Ladder drill (foundation): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Network Policy Validator from a one-paragraph brief.
description:
Drill (FOUNDATION): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Network Policy Validator from a one-paragraph brief

Read the brief twice. List every input the Network Policy Validator needs, every output it must produce, and one contract each input-output pair must satisfy. Work it by hand first, then run the demo program and compare its trace against your own reasoning. When they agree, the concept is yours.

Success criterion: you can list them from memory without looking at the brief
